decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach toward the upright cola bottle with open fingers and small configuration-continuous increments.
Advance the left gripper above the lying bottle toward the cola body; right arm remains parked.
Align the open left fingers around the cola mid-body, slowing the final forward approach.
Fine-center on the cola and close the left gripper; retention will be checked with a short lift.
Lift the closed cola grasp clear of the table, then start carrying it left toward the bin.
Cola is visibly retained; carry it left above the dustbin while keeping the grasp closed.
Cola appears to have slipped toward the table edge. Reopen and approach again rather than assume retention.
Cola is falling within the bin opening. Move the left arm clear toward the remaining left bottles; gently initialize the right arm for the blue bottle.
Approach the central upright white bottle with the left hand. Stage the right hand well apart, avoiding simultaneous contact near the center.
Back the left fingers away slightly, then center the approach on the white bottle without pushing it sideways. Right hand waits clear.
The central bottle has tipped right. Withdraw left upward and prepare a top grasp of the lying left bottle, leaving the right-side bottles to the right hand.
Replan from the interrupted pose using smaller combined translation and wrist-rotation increments to clear the bottles.
Move above the horizontal left bottle and gradually turn the left fingers downward for a top grasp.
Finish turning the left gripper downward and lower toward the left bottle with the jaws open.
Lower slightly around the centered horizontal bottle, close fully, and make a short test lift.
Continue the test lift slowly with the left gripper closed; verify that the horizontal bottle rises and follows.
The bottle stayed on the table. Reopen, re-center, and descend farther so the jaw contact surfaces surround its body rather than only the tips.
Seat the open jaws a little deeper around the horizontal bottle, close fully, and start a small verification lift.
Lift the closed top grasp slowly and move slightly left to check whether the bottle follows.
The left bottle now follows the lift. Carry it toward the bin while raising the right hand clear for a later top grasp.
Carry the left bottle fully over the bin. Move the raised right hand toward the right-side white bottle, rotating gradually downward.
Place the left bottle farther inside the bin opening and release. Continue the right-hand overhead alignment on the white bottle.
Withdraw the empty left hand from the bin; finish the right downward orientation over the white bottle's shoulder for a handover-friendly grasp.
Settle the right jaws around the white bottle shoulder and close; stage the empty left hand on its own side for transfer.
Allow the right gripper to finish closing, then test retention with a gentle lift. Keep left staged and separated.
Verify the right grasp with a slow lift and short inward motion before attempting the handover.
White bottle did not follow the lift. Reopen and align farther toward its visible body center before descending again.
Lower the right contact pads around the white bottle's body and close, keeping the left hand clear.
Test the renewed right grasp with a slow vertical lift before bringing the bottle toward the left receiving hand.
White bottle slipped during the test. Reopen and descend around its updated body center, with deeper pad engagement before another close.
Center the right jaws slightly toward the bottle body after its small shift, then close and allow the fingers to settle.
Keep the right grasp closed through a slow test lift and check the bottle's motion before transferring.
Bring the closed right grasp upward and toward the center while turning the left hand to receive the exposed bottle end from its own side.
The white bottle follows the right hand. Present its left end near the center and align the open left gripper horizontally for handover without crossing the arms.
Replan the interrupted receiving motion with smaller left-arm increments. Keep the right hand stationary and closed on the white bottle.
Slide the open left receiving jaws around the exposed bottle base while leveling the wrist; right continues holding stationary.
Close the left receiving hand on the white bottle base while the right hand continues supporting it; inspect before releasing the donor.
Release the right donor and withdraw it slightly upward while the left receiving grasp remains closed; verify the handover visually.
The transfer slipped onto the table. Reopen and lift the left hand to regrasp the exposed left end from above; withdraw the right toward the blue bottle.
Use much smaller receiving-arm increments after the continuity rejection; both hands reopen and separate for a safer table-assisted recovery.
Approach the white bottle's exposed left end from the left at table height. Align the right hand above the separate blue bottle, keeping the arms apart.
Seat and close the left jaws on the white bottle's exposed end; lower the open right hand toward the blue bottle's body.
Test the left bottle grasp with a slow lift while seating and closing the right fingers around the blue bottle.
The white bottle stayed on the table. Clear the left hand upward and left; test the closed right grasp by lifting the blue bottle.
Replan with much smaller left wrist increments after the zero-execution continuity rejection; slowly lift the right blue-bottle grasp.
Bring the retained blue bottle to the center and align it horizontally; clear and rotate the left receiver toward a top grasp.
Align the angled left receiving jaws with the exposed white end of the blue bottle; keep the right donor stationary and closed.
Seat the left pads slightly farther onto the blue bottle's exposed end, then close while the right hand continues supporting it.
Blue bottle slipped onto the table near center. Separate the hands and prepare a left top grasp on its exposed left end.
Move the left hand over the blue bottle's left end and finish the downward orientation; withdraw the right hand to its own side.
Track the blue bottle's updated position and lower the open left jaws around its white body, remaining left of the centerline.
Correct the left jaw centering toward the bottle visible to the right in the wrist view, then settle gently downward before closing.
Back the left hand clear of the obstructed front-edge grasp. Approach the more accessible white bottle from above with the right hand.
Center the right open jaws on the white bottle body and descend; move the left receiver clear and forward in its own workspace.
Close the right grasp while slightly relieving table contact. Align the left hand for a supported transfer on the left side of the center.
Lift the right-hand white bottle slowly, then bring it toward the middle while the left receiver waits clear.
The bottle remained on the table. Reopen and approach its shoulder more deeply, using the updated visible center rather than assuming a grasp.
Close at the current shoulder contact and allow the grasp to settle before a very small vertical test.
Lift the closed white-bottle grasp and move it toward the center, keeping the left receiver clear until retention is visible.
Present the retained white bottle at the center and align the open left top-grasp on its exposed base, keeping each wrist on its own side.
The wrists are crowding during transfer. Separate the left arm and lower the donor bottle toward the table for a supported handover.
Set the white bottle down across the center, release the donor, and begin withdrawing right so the left can safely receive from the table.
Clear the right donor and position the left downward gripper above the white bottle's left-side body for the supported transfer.
Lower the left open pads around the white bottle's left body, then start closing while the right hand remains clear.
Let the left receiving grasp settle, then verify retention with a slow vertical lift; right remains open and clear.
Carry the closed left white-bottle grasp upward and left while staging the open right hand above the blue bottle's right end.
White bottle visibly follows the left hand; carry it toward the bin. Lower and center the open right jaws over the blue bottle's cap end.
Carry the white bottle farther over the bin so its long free end clears the rim. Seat and close the right grasp on the blue cap section.
Move the white bottle fully inside the rim and release it. Slowly lift the closed blue-bottle grasp to verify retention.
White bottle is descending inside the bin. Reopen the right hand and align on the blue bottle's wider body rather than its cap; withdraw the empty left hand.
Lower the right pads around the blue bottle body and close; bring the left hand back to a separated receiving standby.
Lift the closed blue-bottle grasp gently and move it away from the front obstruction; check that it follows.
Blue bottle is following the right grasp. Bring it forward to the center for a table-supported transfer, while staging the left receiver without wrist contact.
Lower the retained blue bottle onto the central table for a supported handover, then open the donor while the left hand waits clear.
